title: vAttention: Dynamic Memory Management for Serving LLMs without PagedAttention
technique: keep KV cache virtually contiguous but allocate physical memory on demand via CUDA virtual-memory APIs (64KB pages, deferred reclamation, overlapped allocation), so unmodified non-paged attention kernels can be used

optimized_metrics.evidence: Serving LLMs with high throughput requires careful allocation of GPU memory.
optimized_metrics.locator: §2 Background (problem statement; abstract: fragmentation 'crippled the batch size (and consequently throughput)')

optimized_metrics.evidence: PagedAttention ... enables on-demand allocation of GPU memory to mitigate KV cache fragmentation - a phenomenon that crippled the batch size (and consequently throughput) in prior systems. ... physical memory fragmentation can be avoided without making KV cache non-contiguous
such a design leads to non-trivial programming and performance overheads ... vAttention is a simpler, portable ... alternative
optimized_metrics.locator: abstract (qualitative: no kernel rewrite, FA3 supported on day one)

headline_claim.text: improves LLM serving throughput by up to 1.23x compared to the use of PagedAttention-based kernels of FlashAttention-2 and FlashInfer

reported_metrics.where: Fig 7 prefill throughput (prompt tokens/s), Fig 8 decode throughput (tokens/s)
Fig 9 offline requests per minute (427 arXiv-Summarization requests, 64K-192K context)
Fig 10 CDF of end-to-end request execution latency; median reduced up to 42% (online, near capacity)
Table 7 attention kernel latency, Fig 3 kernel sensitivity
Table 3 CUDA VMM API latency vs page size

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We define prefill throughput as the number of prompt tokens processed per second, and decode throughput as the number of tokens generated per second.
metric_definitions.notes: Phase-separated token rates; decode throughput computed 'based on the mean latency of 400 decode iterations' at fixed batch size and 16K initial context (§7.2).

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We measure the end-to-end system throughput in an offline scenario as the number of requests completed per minute.
metric_definitions.notes: Requests/min for long-context (64K-192K) requests, not tokens/s.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We evaluate performance near the serving capacity of the system which denotes the maximum load a system can handle without incurring high queuing delays [35, 51].
metric_definitions.notes: Capacity defined qualitatively (no queueing blow-up); online latency reported as CDF of 'end-to-end request execution latency' with median highlighted.

load_regime: fixed batch sizes (decode micro-benchmarks); offline batch (427 requests); online Poisson QPS near capacity, FCFS (512 requests)
tradeoff_acknowledged: CUDA VMM allocation latency (several ms per call) and 2MB default page granularity risk fragmentation/waste, mitigated by 64KB pages and overlapping allocation with compute; decode throughput only on par with PagedAttention (no gain).
workloads: arXiv-Summarization long-context traces (22K-192K tokens), microbenchmarks at 16K context
extractor_notes: Throughput is phase-specific (prefill tokens/s and decode tokens/s) plus requests/min offline. Online result is reported as median E2E (P50) latency in a CDF; no tail percentile, no TTFT/TPOT. Programmability/portability is a stated co-objective but not numerically measured.
load_class_quote: We measure the end-to-end system throughput in an offline scenario as the number of requests completed per minute (§7.3); online: request arrivals based on Poisson distribution, FCFS (§7.2); decode microbenchmarks at fixed batch sizes (§7.1)
